Trafficked to Myanmar

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
They left for Thailand on the promise of lucrative jobs, now 32 South Africans are stuck in a military compound in Myanmar - the victims of a sophisticated international trafficking syndicate

Unique Selling Point:
We have exclusive access to Lucille Janse Van Vuuren, a 32 year old single mother from Pretoria who fell victim to the traffickers. She is communicating with us from where she is being held on a military compound in Myanmar - one of 7000 thousand victims who were recently rescued from a large scale trafficking operation by a massive crackdown on online scamming sites by the Myanmar authorities. Now, Lucille is stuck in limbo - lured to Thailand under false pretences she was held in Myanmar since July last year and forced to work for the traffickers in online romance scams. But the authorities in Myanmar are refusing to release the South African citizens being held there unless the South African Government steps in to repatriate them. So far the government is silent on the issue, and have not reached out to the South African victims.

Summary:
Lucille was offered a work visa, accommodation and a one year contract to work in sales in Thailand, for a company that needed English speaking employees. Unable to find work in South Africa, she jumped at the opportunity. It took three days to recruit her, and fly her out to Thailand after she responded to an online ad. Her mother dropped her at the airport, while there R10 000 was deposited into her account, and she was told to which gate she had to go to pick up her plane ticket. SA citizens don't need visas to fly to Thailand. Once there, she was escorted by armed men during an 8 hour car drive, had to cross a river at night when no one could see, still under armed guard, and then driven to the "compound" where she would work. The experience left her frightened, and once at the compound her passport was taken and she was told she could not leave because she owed the traffickers money. Then she was forced into working on the scams.

Further information:
I literally got onto the story this morning, so this is a developing situation. We will approach DIRCO for a response.

Trafficked To Myanmar
02 March 2025
FINAL SCRIPT

Intro

Voice

A global underworld run by ruthless gangs…

It’s worth billions of dollars worldwide, and billions more are spent trying to combat it…

Where people are treated as mere commodities, trafficked for profit.

Link Claire
But this story is different. It’s a harrowing account of human trafficking on an industrial scale – revealing how ordinary South Africans fell victim to the ruthless grip of East Asian organized crime syndicates.

Upsound “Amanda”
She’s got her whole life ahead of her.

Upsound Emma van der Walt
We’re talking about modern day slavery.

Upsound Victim Voice Note (Subtitles)
Please, please, please. Please just help us get out.


ACT 1

Voice
This woman - who we’ll call Amanda - is a mother from Krugersdorp. She’s asked us not to use her real name to protect her daughter from victimisation.

Until last year, human trafficking was an unfamiliar concept, something she’d only heard about in movies.

That changed when her daughter accepted a job offer in Thailand, in east Asia.

Upsound “Amanda”
Amanda: She’s a single mom. And she wanted to surprise us, that she can do it, prove it to herself actually more than to us.

Voice
She’d responded to a job offer like this one – aimed at young South Africans with valid passports and good communication skills.


Upsound Amanda
And they say that her voice and her look is perfect for what they want.

Voice
It was supposedly a job in online sales to English speaking customers. To sweeten the deal, Amanda’s daughter was offered free flights and accommodation.

Upsound Amanda
Claire: From the moment she told you until she left, what was that time duration?

Amanda: Three days.

Claire: That’s quick?

Amanda: Three days.

Voice
But, without knowing it, this young South African was falling into a trap, one that’s snared thousands of victims across the globe.

Upsound Emma Van der Walt
It looks amazing, you’re going to find a job in Thailand, you are travelling. And it’s an HR recruitment company, but it’s a false company.

Voice
Emma van der Walt is the founder of Brave to Love, a counter trafficking organisation that’s dealt with similar cases.

Upsound Emma Van der Walt
When they get then to Thailand, that’s when the scary part starts happening.

Voice
Amanda last saw her daughter in July last year.

Upsound Amanda
Myself and her daughter took her to the airport. Within minutes there was money, R10 000 in her card. Half an hour later she had to go through the gates and that was the last we saw her.

Voice
Hours later, her daughter’s excitement at starting a dream job in an exotic country turned into sheer terror. After landing in Thailand, she was forced into a car by armed men, somehow managing to capture this image during the ordeal.

Upsound Emma
At that point she got really scared, she didn’t know where she was.

Voice
What followed was a harrowing nighttime journey across Thailand.

Upsound Emma
They changed cars, vehicles, so many times, she remembers that she travelled 8 hours the first time, then over boat, then changing another 3 to 4 vehicles.

Voice
It’s likely the boat was used to smuggle her across the Moei river into neighbouring Myanmar, a secretive country under military rule since 2021.

Upsound Emma
And then ending up in a scamming compound.

Act 2

Link Claire
Most trafficking victims are condemned to lives of grueling labour or sold into sexual exploitation. But in this case, they’ve been coerced into becoming the criminals themselves.

Voice
They’re called scam compounds – large apartment buildings scattered along the border between Myanmar and Thailand. Often controlled by members of the Chinese mafia. Victims who are lured here are forced into defrauding others online – typically in romance scams – where scammers pretend to be romantically interested in victims to exploit them financially.

Upsound Mina Chiang (Subtitles)
Sometimes in one single compound, you might find 3000 or 4000 people. And they’re being treated as slaves, and they’re being treated as victims of human trafficking, being forced against their will to conduct those online scams.

Voice
London based Mina Chiang provides investigative and consultancy services to governments and NGO’s.

Upsound Mina Chiang (Subtitles)
They are particularly powerful. So that means they have good connections, they have weapons, they have their militia.

Voice
Amanda’s daughter, along with at least 32 other South Africans, ended up in what is reported to be one of the worst scam sites, the so-called KK Compound.

Upsound Mina Chiang (Subtitles)
This is one of the largest and most powerful compounds, so over the years if you look at the satellite images you might see that actually it’s expanding.

Voice
A victim currently being held captive in a section of the massive KK Compound known as KK4, has been secretly sending us voice notes.

Upsound Victim Voicenote (Subtitles)
A lot of people are too scared to speak to anybody else, we’ve been trying to get some form of help from the embassy, they also say that they can’t help us.

Voice
Like thousands of others, the South Africans lured to KK Compound had their passports confiscated and were threatened with violence unless they agreed to participate in the scamming.

Upsound Amanda
She cried, and she said they’re taking people’s life savings. And once the people have given their life savings, because you’re in love and you’re trying to help this person, you just disappear. And then what they do is they bang on a gong and there’s a big party once they’ve achieved a goal.

Voice
Her daughter refused to participate in the scams – so the bosses forced her into scouring the internet for possible victims. But not before making an example of her.

Upsound Amanda
She got punished at one stage. I don’t know how she got punished, she won’t talk about it. She goes dead quiet.

Voice
Trapped in a foreign country notorious for human rights abuses, and threatened with violence or jail time if they don’t comply, victims are left with little choice.

Upsound Emma
They are forced to do criminality, they are forced to do online scams.

Voice
About two weeks ago, there was news for Amanda.

More than 7000 of an estimated 100 000 victims along the Thai-Myanmar border were freed by one of the many militia groups active in the country since a military coup in 2021.

Her daughter was one of those saved, but she’s still not free.

Upsound Amanda
They keep threatening them, if you phone anybody, we’re going to take your phone away.

Voice
Our source inside Myanmar told us that people are confined to their rooms, the militia unwilling to let them go unless the South African government makes contact.

Upsound Victim Voice Note (Subtitles)
Please, please, please. Please just help us get out.

Voice
After contacting the South African embassy for help, and being stone-walled, Amanda got hold of Emma van der Walt.

Upsound Amanda
I need her to come home, she’s got her whole life ahead of her, and nobody wants to help.

Voice
Nor, it seems, does anyone know who’s in charge on the ground in Myanmar – where victims from almost 30 countries are currently being detained. We approached the Department of International Relations and Cooperation for answers.

Upsound Clayson Monyela
The authorities in Thailand insist that before they can receive them on the Thailand side, they need to have flight tickets to return to South Africa amongst other things.

Voice
Clayson Monyela, from the Department of International Cooperation, says government policy doesn’t allow financial aid to the victims. The current delay is in part because funds need to be raised for flights back to South Africa.

Upsound Clayson
So we’re talking to everybody, to try and cover the rest of the South Africans who don’t have the means to get their own flight tickets.

Voice
According to our sources, many of the victims in Myanmar fear being arrested by the Thai authorities.

Upsound Clayson
So that fear from them, whilst valid, we can assure them that there has been a conversation that they would not be arrested.

Act 3

Voice
There are growing concerns of a possible humanitarian crisis in Myanmar – the militias are struggling with the numbers.

Upsound Emma
Emma: There’s a very strong possibility that the victims can be handed back to the Chinese bosses, back into the scamming, back into slavery.

Upsound Amanda
It’s always happening on movies, this is real, this is happening, now, to us as a family. There’s no Liam Neeson to go out and do what he needs to do.

Voice
In the absence of a real-life action hero, the fates of 32 victims now lie squarely in the hands of government.






PROMOS
Promo 1

Voice
They left for Thailand on the promise of lucrative jobs and better lives.

Upsound Emma
They are forced to do criminality; they are forced to do online scams. We are talking about modern day slavery.

Voice
But now 32 South Africans are stuck in limbo, after being trafficked to Myanmar by ruthless criminals.


Promo 2

Voice
Saved from the clutches of brutal scam compounds in Myanmar, 32 South Africans now face a new nightmare.

Upsound Amanda
I need her to come home, she’s got her whole life ahead of her, and nobody wants to help.

Voice
Can the government bring them home?


Promo 3
Voice
They fell victim to organized crime syndicates from Myanmar who lured them to Asia with false promises.

Upsound Emma
Emma: There’s a very strong possibility that the victims can be handed back to the bosses, back into slavery.

Voice
Now a group of South Africans are among thousands of victims desperately seeking repatriation.
